content.text: In classical logic, a contradiction implies everything. This is the **principle of explosion**.
Paraconsistent logics block explosion, so a contradiction stays local instead of making every statement provable.

examples.title: Explosion
examples.note: B can be anything at all.

examples.title: Why block it
lines: A large database holds two records that contradict each other.
examples.note: We still want to reason with the rest, without one error making everything true.

question.prompt: What does a paraconsistent logic reject?
question.hint: What happens to everything else in classical logic once a contradiction appears?
question.explanation: Paraconsistent logic rejects explosion, the rule that a contradiction implies every statement.
